import.title: Import LangGraph repo
import.desc: Clones the repo, installs dependencies into its own venv and reads graphs from langgraph.json (or scans compiled StateGraphs).
import.warning: The repo's code will be executed (in a subprocess + its own venv, not a full sandbox). Only import repos you trust.
import.requiredEnvHint: set them in the server env to run.

human.title: Waiting for your response
human.placeholder: Type a response, or approve / reject
human.pendingDesc: Runs paused at a Human node

api.title: Trigger via API
api.desc: Start this workflow from other systems with a per-workflow token. Runs appear in history with source API.
api.copyOnce: Copy the token now; it is shown only once.
api.name: Token name
api.modes: mode "sync" waits for the result; "async" (default) returns 202 with run_id — poll GET …/runs/{run_id} or pass callback_url to receive the result.
api.signingHelp: Callbacks carry X-Studio-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<body>")>. Verify it and reject old timestamps (see README).
api.rotated: New signing secret. The previous one keeps signing callbacks until {{when}}, so receivers can switch over.

versions.title: Version history
versions.desc: Every save that changes the workflow creates a version. Compare any two, or restore an older one as a new version.
versions.restored: Restored v{{n}} as a new version.
versions.unchanged: v{{n}} is identical to the current version, so nothing was restored.
versions.unsavedWarning: You have unsaved changes in the editor. Restoring replaces them.

notifyPrefs.title: Notification settings
notifyPrefs.description: Choose how you hear about runs that wait for you or expire.
notifyPrefs.in_appHelp: Show notifications in the bell, live as they happen.
notifyPrefs.emailHelp: Send an e-mail to your account address.
notifyPrefs.emailNotConfigured: E-mail is not set up on this server (SMTP_HOST), so no e-mails are sent yet.

approvals.keepSecret: Saved, enter a new value to replace

help.slack: Create a Slack app with the bot scopes chat:write and im:write (verification codes), turn on Interactivity with the Request URL shown on the connection. Each workspace is its own connection.
help.telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather, save its token, then register the webhook (needs a public https STUDIO_PUBLIC_URL).

approvals.publicUrlMissing: STUDIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set: the platform must reach this server at a public https address.
approvals.identitiesHelp: Link your chat accounts so a button you press in Slack or Telegram counts as you. Slack accounts are linked per workspace. The bot sends a one-time code to the account; type it here to verify. Only the run owner and the approvers listed on the Human node can approve.

identityHow.slack: Slack: your profile → ⋮ → Copy member ID.
identityHow.telegram: Telegram: message @userinfobot to see your numeric ID.

node.title: Approval channel
node.connectFirst: No usable connection. Add one in Settings → Channels (or ask an admin for an organization one).
node.approversHelp: Besides you (the run owner). They must link and verify their account under My accounts.

approvals.codeSent: Enter the 6-digit code the bot sent you
approvals.codeNeeded: Send a code to verify this account
approvals.telegramStart: Telegram bots can only message you after you press Start in the bot chat.
approvals.name: Name
approvals.noChannels: No connections yet. Add your own Slack app or Telegram bot below.
approvals.orgReadOnly: Managed by an admin. You can pick it on your Human nodes.
approvals.sharedHelp: One Interactivity URL for every Slack workspace; requests are routed by the workspace ID ({{team}}) and checked with this app's signing secret.

settings.title: Settings

intro.channels: Approve or reject waiting runs from Slack or Telegram. Tokens are stored encrypted.
intro.accounts: Your chat accounts. A button press counts as you only after the account is verified with a one-time code.
intro.audit: Every approval request and decision made through a chat channel.
intro.knowledge: Documents that Retriever nodes search. Text is split into chunks and embedded; only you can use your knowledge bases.
intro.mcp: Tools from Model Context Protocol servers, used by MCP tool nodes. Secrets are encrypted and never shown again.

platform.slack: Buttons in a Slack channel. One connection per workspace.
platform.telegram: Buttons in a Telegram group or private chat, through your bot.

scopeHelp.org: Organization connections are set up by an admin and usable by everyone.
scopeHelp.user: Personal connections are only usable on your own workflows.

settings.orgAskAdmin: No organization connection yet. Ask an admin to add one.
settings.myAccountsHelp: Link and verify your account so your button presses count.
settings.noAccountSlot: Add a connection first to link your account.

kb.newHelp: Give it a name, then upload documents.
kb.name: Name
kb.embedHelp: Without a key the server's OPENAI_API_KEY is used, or a deterministic offline embedding. Changing the model or key re-indexes the documents.
kb.confirmDelete: Delete the knowledge base "{{name}}" and all its documents?

mcp.newHelp: Streamable HTTP endpoint, or a local command (stdio) when the server allows it.
mcp.name: Name
mcp.secretHelp: Values are encrypted on the server and never shown again. A stdio server sees only these variables, not the studio's environment.
mcp.confirmDelete: Delete the MCP server "{{name}}"? Nodes that use it will fail.
mcp.stdioOn: stdio servers are enabled: admins can register local commands. They run on the studio host with a clean environment, an empty temporary home directory and a time limit, but no further isolation: only add commands you trust, or run the studio in a container.
mcp.stdioOff: stdio servers are disabled on this server (STUDIO_MCP_STDIO=1 enables them for admins). HTTP servers must use public addresses unless STUDIO_MCP_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1.
